clue.text: Changed doctor provided, that is, daughters come round

indicators.note: to come round something is to surround it, so the daughters wrap themselves about the words before

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a standard crossword doctor
D is daughter, so two daughters give two Ds
'provided' as in 'on condition that'
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A doctor's plans were altered because the daughters came round to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come round' looks like a visit, but it tells the two daughters to surround the middle pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something is to alter it, so modified is a past-tense synonym for altered.

clue.text: Notice jumpers are going up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: jumpers (sweaters) are tops

explanation.surface: A shopper sees that the price of sweaters is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, the verb sense of notice.

clue.text: Leave unfinished line about king being eccentric

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so the line encircles the king
something unfinished is missing its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to quit is to leave
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a half-written line about a monarch for being odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' is not verse here but a railway, abbreviated as it is on maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Quirky behaviour is odd and unconventional, which is what eccentric describes.

clue.text: At your send-off, bishop and I included a short life history

indicators.note: included means placed inside the other letters
sending something off scatters it, so the preceding letters are dispatched into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: At your funeral, a bishop and I read out a brief account of your life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send-off' looks like part of the funeral picture, but it scrambles AT YOUR, into which B and I are placed.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a newspaper notice summarising the career and achievements of someone recently dead.

clue.text: Bolt maybe a variety of beans after a period without eating

indicators.note: after tells us the beans come later in the entry than the eating period

parts.note: a fast is a time of going without food
runner beans are a type of climbing bean

explanation.surface: Someone bolts down a plate of beans after a long fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt is not gobbling food but Usain Bolt, the Jamaican sprinter; 'maybe' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Usain Bolt, the Olympic sprint champion, is a famous example of a speedy athlete.

clue.text: Physical training keeps pin-up flexible

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for physical training

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a nail is a kind of pin

explanation.surface: Gym workouts keep a pin-up model supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliant bends easily without breaking, the same quality as being flexible.

clue.text: Blend egg in cake mixture initially, then beat

indicators.note: then says the next piece follows on
in places the egg inside the other letters
initially points to the opening letter of each word

parts.note: first letters of cake and mixture
an egg is round, like the letter O
to pound is to beat

explanation.surface: A baking instruction: fold the egg into the cake mix, then beat it.
explanation.walkthrough: C(O)M + POUND; 'Blend' is the noun, a mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound is a mixture of several elements, so a blend is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Hesitate to free up article trapped inside

indicators.note: something trapped inside is enclosed by the outer letters
in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to rid is to free
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates to release a thing that has got stuck inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to waver indecisively, unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Live long, occupying time with dog

parts.note: to be is to live, exist

indicators.note: to occupy something is to sit inside it

parts.note: an age is a period of time
L is a standard abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: Wishing someone and their dog long life together.
explanation.walkthrough: BE + AG(L)E: the abbreviation for long sits inside the word for a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hound breed used for hunting hares.

clue.text: Brand-new moneymaker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in perfect, unused condition
second meaning: the place where coins are produced

explanation.surface: A fresh, profitable venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint condition means pristine, and the Royal Mint is the official factory where coins are struck.

clue.text: Knock art made with a couple of bits of junk

indicators.note: something made has been fashioned, so these letters are reshaped into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
tat is cheap junk, and a couple means two lots of it

explanation.surface: Artwork knocked together from a few scraps of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tat is British slang for tasteless or worthless odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat-a-tat-tat imitates the repeated sound of rapping on a door.

clue.text: Good-natured sort left legacy behind

parts.note: a kind is a sort or type
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: behind points to the tail end of the word, its final letter

parts.note: last letter of legacy

explanation.surface: A generous relative who left a bequest behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: A kindly person is warm, gentle and considerate, which is what good-natured means.

clue.text: Silly son's 50-50 after exercises, having a funny turn

indicators.note: after places the even split later than the exercises

parts.note: dizzy can mean scatterbrained, silly
S is the abbreviation for son
PE is physical education, school exercises
L is the Roman numeral 50, so 50-50 is two Ls

explanation.surface: A daft boy's even chances, after a workout, of collapsing in a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: A funny turn is a British phrase for a brief bout of feeling faint.
explanation.definitionFit: A dizzy spell is a short episode of light-headedness, the sudden queasy fit the phrase describes.

clue.text: Reckon online price cut has affected tea

parts.note: E as in e-commerce, electronic or online

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so its letters are moved around
something cut has been trimmed short, losing its end

parts.note: a price is a value
the letters to be rearranged, taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper reckons an online discount has changed what they pay for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to assess or calculate, the same as reckoning up a figure.

clue.text: Impress daughter with cool music, starting off with the French

indicators.note: with its start taken off, the first letter goes

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
jazz is cool music
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A girl wows the crowd with cool tunes, opening with a French number.
explanation.definitionFit: To dazzle someone is to amaze them with brilliance, so it means to impress greatly.

clue.text: Songwriter's catalogue includes riches, half unknown before

indicators.note: to include is to hold inside

parts.note: a list is a catalogue

indicators.note: half means only part of the word survives, the rest dropped
before puts the unknown ahead of the rich half

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
taken as written, then halved

explanation.surface: A composer's back catalogue holds wealth from an anonymous early hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps the first three of the six letters; the 's after Songwriter stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyricist writes the words of songs, so is a kind of songwriter.

clue.text: Caught and gently treated missing large young bird

indicators.note: something treated has been processed, so these letters are worked into a new order
missing means a letter is absent from the word

parts.note: C is caught in cricket scoring
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A rescued chick is caught and handled carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of GENTLY, rearrange GENTY and put C in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a baby swan, a juvenile of one of the largest birds.

clue.text: Scrupulous but informal with thug

parts.note: tho is the casual spelling of though, meaning but
a rough is a hooligan or thug

explanation.surface: Careful, but casual in dealing with a heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough person is meticulous and attends to every detail, the quality called scrupulous.

clue.text: Heartily enjoy mum's sisters' outings

indicators.note: heartily points to the heart, the central letter of the word

parts.note: middle letter of enjoy
your mother's sisters are your aunts

explanation.surface: Mum's sisters thoroughly love their days out.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunts are short pleasure trips or excursions, which is what outings are.

clue.text: Retirement home where things are unclear?

definitions.text: Retirement home where things are unclear?

parts.note: setter's reading: a place full of grey-haired pensioners
the real meaning: a situation with no clear-cut rules

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for an old-folks' home where residents are muddled; read with grey as grey-haired, the phrase also names the territory between black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation that is ambiguous and not clearly covered by existing rules.

clue.text: Gunners side taking international trophy borders on strangeness

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
R is right, one side
I is the abbreviation for international

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters of trophy

explanation.surface: Arsenal (the Gunners) winning an international cup would be a bizarre event.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal football club is nicknamed the Gunners, but here the word means the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarity is the quality of being uncommon or unusual, which overlaps with strangeness.

clue.text: Abandon castle when king's left protected by another piece

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded by its guard

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts

indicators.note: when the king has left, that letter is gone from the word

parts.note: the castle in chess is the rook
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A chess move: give up the castle once the king has moved, guarded by another piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To maroon someone is to leave them stranded somewhere, abandoned with no escape.

clue.text: One's quiet about plan's unhappy outcome

indicators.note: about here means surrounded, with the plan wrapped round the pieces before it

parts.note: a plan or diagram is a map
one is the Roman numeral I
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent about how their scheme went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Both apostrophe-esses are padding for the surface and give no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident, an unfortunate result of some action.

clue.text: Bagpipe pieces include works about Scotch pancakes

indicators.note: to include is to hold within

parts.note: the drones are the pipes on a bagpipe that sound a constant note
ops is short for opera, musical works
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A Scottish breakfast scene with bagpipes playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop scones are small thick pancakes, a British teatime treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop scones are made by dropping batter on a griddle, and are known as Scotch pancakes.

clue.text: Swear love in a Volkswagen

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places one thing inside the other

parts.note: VW is the Volkswagen badge
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A couple pledge their devotion in a VW car.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare or assert solemnly, the sense of swear.

clue.text: Top copy with ten underneath

indicators.note: in a down entry, underneath puts this piece lower, after the other

parts.note: to ape is to copy
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A top-of-the-class copy with a score of ten below it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: One plays records from America following brief trend

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing the last letter
following puts America after the trend

parts.note: a style is a fashion or trend
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A DJ spins American discs following a short-lived craze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One plays records' sounds like a DJ, but it is the needle of a record player.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is the gramophone needle that runs in the groove and reproduces the sound of vinyl.

clue.text: Forage in underground chamber cutting tin and germanium

indicators.note: cutting into something means going between its letters

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a cave is an underground chamber
Ge is the chemical symbol for germanium

explanation.surface: Searching for food in a cave among deposits of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge is to search around for usable food or items, which is what foraging involves.
